territorial_scope.description: A federal criminal offence reaching conduct in interstate or foreign commerce, while platform duties apply to covered platforms serving the public.

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Makes knowingly publishing nonconsensual intimate visual depictions, including deepfakes, a federal crime and requires covered online platforms to create notice-and-removal processes and remove flagged depictions within 48 hours of a valid request; the FTC enforces the platform duties.
summary.long: Adds section 223(h) to the Communications Act of 1934, making it a federal offence to knowingly publish, via an interactive computer service in interstate or foreign commerce, a nonconsensual intimate visual depiction of an identifiable individual; deepfakes are covered. Publication of depictions of adults requires harm or intent to harm; depictions of minors require intent to abuse, humiliate, harass, degrade or sexually gratify. Penalties are up to 2 years' imprisonment for adult offences and 3 years for minor offences, plus fines; threats are punished alike, and courts must order forfeiture and restitution. Law-enforcement, good-faith reporting and medical or educational disclosures are excepted. Covered platforms (public services primarily hosting user-generated content, excluding broadband, email and mainly preselected content) must, within one year of enactment, set up a removal-request process with clear notice, and remove reported depictions and identical copies within 48 hours of a valid request. Platforms are not liable for claims arising from good-faith removal of apparently unlawful material. The FTC enforces platform duties as violations of a rule on unfair or deceptive practices.
